page: Amazon Web Services r8g.4xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the custom AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 processor built on the arm64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz with no hyperthreading. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, lacks local storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the strong memory subsystem of this instance. The Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier (top 10%), supported by strong uncached memory bandwidth performance, reaching 317.2 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 130.27 GB/sec for large block write operations. Compute performance is solid, with Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Database operations also demonstrate strong performance, with Passmark database operations scoring 23912.07. However, the instance shows limitations in heavy AI workloads, with LLM inference for large models registering poor performance at 2.37 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r8g.4xlarge offers a highly dense memory profile on custom Arm-based silicon, which typically delivers favorable performance-per-watt and resource density compared to traditional x86 architectures. Because it lacks local storage and dedicated GPU hardware, it is not designed for local storage-heavy or hardware-accelerated graphics workloads. Instead, the instance is optimized for memory-intensive applications, including high-throughput database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, data processing pipelines, and memory-bound enterprise applications.
